haiku-low.q1: It gets a 401 Unauthorized. The rate-limit store is never touched, so no counter changes.
haiku-low.q2: Standard customers get 100 per minute in total. Counters use the customer ID, not the API key, so the three keys share one limit.
haiku-low.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit, and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. The backend never sees the request.
haiku-low.q4: No. A DENY does not increment the count, so the rejected request uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The count is incremented before forwarding and never rolled back, so the failed request still uses budget.
haiku-low.q6: The gateway forwards the request, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and sends no X-RateLimit headers. It does not retry.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is undecided, with no limit set, so its requests are unlimited, uncounted, and get no headers.
haiku-low.q8: Counts live in one shared Redis instance with a replica, keyed by customer and minute window. Keys expire 120 seconds after the first increment.
haiku-low.q9: The budget resets at each clock-aligned one-minute window, since a new key starts at zero. Old keys expire after 120 seconds.
haiku-low.q10: The Lua script runs to completion on Redis as a single step, so concurrent requests from different instances cannot overshoot.
haiku-low.q11: It is the seconds until the current window ends, rounded up, and never less than 1.
haiku-low.q12: No retry happens. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers, since the real values are unknown.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized (also for a missing key). The rate-limit store is never touched, so no counter is affected.
sonnet.q2: The same as one customer's limit (e.g. 100/min for Standard), because the counter is keyed by customer ID from the Key Service, not by API key. Total is shared across all three keys.
sonnet.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After, plus X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
sonnet.q4: No. On DENY the count is not incremented.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The count is incremented before forwarding and never rolled back, so a backend 500 still uses budget.
sonnet.q6: It fails open. The gateway forwards the request, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, sends no X-RateLimit-* headers, and does not retry.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is undecided (OPEN) and the table entry is unset, so Enterprise requests skip the rate-limit check today (unlimited).
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis instance (with a replica for failover), under key rl:{customerId}:{floor(now/60)}. The key expires 120 s after the first increment, which removes old counts.
sonnet.q9: Fixed one-minute clock-aligned windows. When the next window starts, the key changes, so the count starts fresh from zero. Retry-After gives the seconds until the window ends.
sonnet.q10: The gateway calls a single Lua script on Redis that reads the count, denies or increments in one step. Redis runs a script to completion before the next one, so two instances cannot both see 99 and both pass.
sonnet.q11: Seconds until the current window ends, rounded up, never below 1. The script returns the seconds left in the window, computed from Redis TIME.
sonnet.q12: No retry. The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers, only the unchanged backend response. If the script still ran after the gateway gave up, its increment is kept.
